name: gate
wording: A point at a handover where the work stops for the operator's sign-off: a story's read-back, held by the architect; a story's plan read-back, held by the lead, which a task with no story skips unless the operator calls it; a pull request the operator reviews, held by the lead before it merges; release; a fork that is irreversible, about value or beyond the architect's competence; and any point the operator calls, stop included. A gate is held in the session of the party whose handover it is, which ends its turn there, its reply ending with the sign-off it waits on, until the operator answers. The operator is told, in the session it works in, as soon as a gate waits on it, which party holds it and where to join it, and joins that session there. The party that delegated the work takes no part in it: of what passes there, nothing reaches its own context by any route, a summary it later reads included, beyond the fact that the work waits on the operator, and then the result; a record it never reads is not learning. Pushing a branch or opening a pull request is never a gate, and between gates the agents work without checking in.
reason: A pull request held at a gate in a delegate's session waited on the operator with no word reaching the operator or the party that delegated the work: a gate the operator is not told of holds nothing. The operator is told, where it works, as soon as one waits on it.
